passage:
On Monday Sonali opened the class group chat and saw a meme with her face pasted onto a cartoon pig. Her cheeks burned. More laughing faces kept arriving. She took a screenshot, blocked the sender and told her mother that night.

Then an account with no name began sending nasty messages. Sonali caught herself staring at ten possible classmates, testing each guess. Zubin said, "Do not do that. Let us report it." They saved the messages and reported the account to the platform and to the school counsellor next morning. The counsellor promised to speak to the class teacher the same day.

Sonali's first impulse was to post a nastier meme in return. She typed half of it, then deleted it. Revenge would only feed the fire, she thought, and the screenshots were better.

By Wednesday her stomach cramped whenever she saw the school gate. She told her mother, "I don't want to go." Her mother sat beside her, did not argue, and phoned the school office. The next day the counsellor met Sonali with the head. Tanvir sat with her at lunch. "This is not your fault." By Friday the account was closed.

qa.q: What was Sonali's face pasted onto in the meme?
qa.a: It was pasted onto a cartoon pig.

qa.q: How did Sonali's first impulse after the meme differ from what she actually did about the anonymous account and her dread of school?
qa.a: She wanted to post a nastier meme, but she deleted it, saved screenshots, reported the account with Zubin, and told her mother and the counsellor about her dread.

qa.q: What was Sonali feeling when her stomach cramped at the sight of the school gate?
qa.a: She felt dread and fear about going to school because of what was online.

qa.q: What did Zubin suggest when Sonali stared at possible classmates?
qa.a: Zubin suggested reporting the account instead of guessing who it was.

grounding: One teenager is mocked with memes and messages from an anonymous account, feels angry and afraid, and turns to evidence, reporting and trusted adults.
